page.layout: One printed page of running text in a single column. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. Torn or stained left edge with fragments of text in the left margin, which I have not transcribed as notes. No other margin text, catchword or signature.

main_text.p: idem, quod haud levis momenti erat, non erat reddendis rationibus obnoxius: quod quidem Aristoteles velut modum reipublicæ liberæ excedens, & iniquis desideriis frenum laxans, in hac νομοθεσία[?] Lycurgi, quemadmodum & quædam alia, reprehendit. Ius autem surrogandi senatores in loca eorum, qui aut morte, aut culpa sua, aut casu alio ea vacua essent facturi, non regibus, non ipsi senatui, sed soli concilio totius populi, quod ἐκκλησίαν[?] Græci dicebant, concionem Latinè interpretamur, idem legislator tribuit. Hoc vero in eo cavit, ne quisquam nisi petens, & se populo in comitiis offendens, nec nisi virtute præstans, legitimæque ætatis, surrogaretur: surrogatus ut omnium ordinum gaudio & congratulatione & honore exciperetur, ac velut in possessionem dignitatis mitteretur. At concionis hujus convocandæ & regendæ dimittendæque potestatem ex eadem, quam dixi, rethrà Delphicâ regibus & senatui dedit: qua concione nihil omnino fuit in omnibus ipsius institutis popularius: cui posteris sæculis etiam ad augendam ejus majestatem multò plura accesserunt, de quibus posteà dicemus. Cætera sic constituit. Primum ut invidiæ, odii, discordiæ matrem ac nu-tricem

page.notes: The left edge is damaged: fragments such as "gau", "ir" and "ur" stand beside the lines "virtute" and "surrogaretur", and are not printed text of this page. The Greek words νομοθεσία and ἐκκλησίαν are read with doubt and marked [?]; the accents may differ from the printed ones. The word "eadem" at the line end is followed by a mark that may be a hyphen or a blot. "rethrà" is copied as printed. The small marks at the top right edge are show-through or edge, and are not transcribed.
